newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Belgium to resume cooperation with new Congo.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to resume cooperation with new Congo.

text.p: A Belgian minister, winding up a three-day official visit to the Congolese capital Kinshasa, said on Friday that Belgium and Congo have agreed to resume bilateral cooperation in the near future.

Reginald Moreels, state secretary for cooperation and development, told a news conference that Belgium would emphasise "good governance" and respect for human rights by the authorities in the renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo.

"The resumption of structural and institutional cooperation (with Congo) must materialise in the (near) future. Structural and institutional assistance will be in place in the next months, the next years," Moreels said.

"The political context of the (new) cooperation will take into account good governance and human rights," he said, adding that the Congolese authorities were keen to improve the country's human rights record.
Moreels said this new type of cooperation will target education, health, agriculture and justice in the Congo. But he declined to reveal financial figures for the assistance.
He said that both partners would be committed to mutually respecting each other. The Congo is a former Belgian colony.

"I refuse to announce figures. It's no longer the complex of donor and recipient," Moreels said. "The era of paternalism, colonialsm and neo-colonialism is finished. Belgium has opted for the policy of presence (in the new Congo)."
He denounced the "lack of state" and corruption under the 32-year reign of dictator Mobutu Sese Seko, toppled in May by rebels under Laurent Kabila, who is now president.
Belgium cut direct aid to Mobutu's Zaire following the alleged massacres of students at Lubumbashi University in 1990.
But Belgium has continued to channel funds into the vast central African country through non-governmental organisations.
Diplomatic sources told Reuters that Belgium was prepared to fund 250 projects designed by Congolese NGOs.
"The funding will necessitate about 3 billion Belgian francs ($78.7 million)," one diplomat said.
Moreels is the first senior Western government official to have set foot on Congolese soil since Kabila replaced Mobutu in May after a seven-month military campaign.
Relations between the former Zaire and Belgium were cool during the Mobutu era. ($ = 38.12 Belgian Francs)
